sources.use: Existing product, architecture, pricing, treasury, risk, and financial assumptions
Core value, requirements, validation gates, pricing, constraints, and decisions
Prior phase roadmap and completion claims
Distribution, moat, target user, exclusions, and assumptions

methods: Read existing planning and master-plan files
Inspected current app, API, worker, and Prisma file tree

businessThesis.current: CivicState is a watchlist civic-tech product that sells one-time researched, citation-backed constituent letters for $5, $15, and $25 [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md; apps/web/app/page.tsx].
businessThesis.why: The repo has real product implementation evidence, but no repo evidence of paid demand, live deliverability, attorney review, payment processor stability, or production conversion [evidence: repository file scan, 2026-06-21].
businessThesis.operatorConstraint: Registry note says personal/research asset and asks operator to confirm whether it should pitch as a business [evidence: dispatch registry notes, 2026-06-21].

customerDefinition.primaryCustomer: Individual United States resident with a specific civic issue who wants help researching, drafting, routing, and delivering a constituent letter [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
nonCustomers: Businesses seeking advocacy in entity capacity [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
Legal claimants or users seeking filings [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
Bulk campaigners and harassment/defamation-risk users [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]

marketSizing.launchAudience: 10,000 high-intent annual civic-letter buyers [assumption: conservative validation scenario, not sourced market data]
marketSizing.averageOrderValue: $15 [assumption: midpoint of $5, $15, and $25 repo tiers; evidence for tiers: .planning/PROJECT.md]

costInputs: $0.10 to $0.40 AI cost per submission [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
about $96 per month backend droplet [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
$50 per month Postmark card limit [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
revenueModel.reconciliation: Revenue table in BUSINESS.md reconciles paid submissions multiplied by AOV to revenue and subtracts high-end AI cost plus fixed platform costs [assumption: simplified model excludes Stripe fees, labor, legal, refunds, tax, and acquisition].

motions: Recruit at least 30 paid civic issue submitters [assumption: early validation sample].
Validate at least 85% inbox placement on government domains [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Publish only opt-in, privacy-safe campaign pages and track 90-day search impressions [assumption: SEO validation window; evidence for SEO strategy: .planning/GENESIS.md].
Keep paid acquisition, partnerships, subscriptions, API access, certified mail, fax, and community features deferred [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md; MASTER_PLAN.md].

risksAntiPlan.antiPlan: The project may be useful but not venture-worthy: users may not pay for something they can do by email, officials may ignore or suppress AI-written letters, legal review may constrain the citation-backed promise, payment processors may flag civic content, and SEO may not compound from sparse opt-in local pages [assumption: skeptic case based on repo risks and product model].

holes.mitigation: Run concierge beta with paid submissions and refund tracking
holes.residualRisk: Users may prefer free templates or direct email

holes.mitigation: Use SPF/DKIM/DMARC, Postmark warming, bounce monitoring, and inbox tests [evidence: scripts/setup-dns.md]
holes.residualRisk: Government domains may still filter or complain

holes.mitigation: Review terms, AI disclosure, CAN-SPAM posture, citation language, and moderation policy
holes.residualRisk: The product promise may need to be narrowed

holes.mitigation: Root soul now flags stale planning contradictions
holes.residualRisk: Data room remains confusing until planning artifacts are reconciled
